title: Switchboard
story: Six switches (1 = ON, 0 = OFF) control the vault. Their gates are described below.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Every switch is either 0 or 1.
Switch 1 is OFF.
Switch 2 XOR switch 3 = 0 (they match).
Switch 3 XOR switch 4 = 1 (they differ).
Switch 5 is NOT switch 4.
Switch 6 is switch 1 OR switch 4.
Exactly three switches are ON.

explanation: If switch 2 = 1: switches 2, 3, 5 are ON, 4 and 6 are OFF: 0 1 1 0 1 0, three ON. If switch 2 = 0: 0 0 0 1 0 1 has only two ON, so it fails. Code: 011010. The code is 011010.
steps: If switch 2 = 1: switches 2, 3, 5 are ON, 4 and 6 are OFF: 0 1 1 0 1 0, three ON.
If switch 2 = 0: 0 0 0 1 0 1 has only two ON, so it fails.
hints: Switch 1 is OFF. What does that make switch 6?
Everything depends on switch 2. Try it ON, then try it OFF, and count the ON switches.
Near the end: the code starts with 01 and ends with 0. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Mirror Alphabet
story: A message in a mirrored alphabet appears: HRC VRTSG GDL ULFI MRMV AVIL.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The alphabet is mirrored (A becomes Z, B becomes Y, ...). Decode each word; each word is a number.
The code is those six numbers in order.

explanation: Decoded: SIX, EIGHT, TWO, FOUR, NINE, ZERO. Code: 682490. The code is 682490.
steps: Decoded: SIX, EIGHT, TWO, FOUR, NINE, ZERO.
hints: A and Z swap, B and Y swap. What does H become?
H -> S, R -> I, C -> X. Do the same for every word.
Near the end: the code starts with 68 and ends with 0. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Counting Ways
story: The vault wants three counts.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: the number of handshakes if 12 people each shake hands once with everyone else.
Middle pair: the number of ways to pick 2 people from 9.
Last pair: the number of different arrangements of the letters AABB.

explanation: C(12,2) = 66, C(9,2) = 36, AABB arrangements = 6. The code is 663606.
hints: Each handshake is a pair of people. Order within a pair does not matter.
Pairs from n: n(n-1)/2. Arrangements of AABB: 4! divided by 2! twice.
Near the end: the code starts with 66 and ends with 6. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Quarter Turn
story: A grid of digits will be turned by the vault.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Rotate the grid a quarter turn clockwise. The code is the first two rows of the rotated grid, read left to right.

explanation: Rotated rows: 814 / 390 / 527. Code: 814390. The code is 814390.
hints: The left column becomes the top row.
After a clockwise turn, the top row is the old left column read bottom to top.
Near the end: the code starts with 81 and ends with 0. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: The Invariant
story: A board holds numbers. A move erases two numbers a and b and writes a + b + a x b in their place. Moves repeat until one number remains.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Board one: 1, 2, 3, 4. Board two: 1, 1, 2, 3. Whatever order you choose, the final number is always the same for a given board.
The code is board one's final number followed by board two's final number, each as three digits with leading zeros.

explanation: Product of (x + 1) over the board never changes. Board one: 2 x 3 x 4 x 5 = 120, final 119. Board two: 2 x 2 x 3 x 4 = 48, final 47 = 047. Code: 119047. The code is 119047.
steps: Product of (x + 1) over the board never changes.
Board one: 2 x 3 x 4 x 5 = 120, final 119. Board two: 2 x 2 x 3 x 4 = 48, final 47 = 047.
hints: Try the moves in two different orders on board one.
Notice that a + b + ab + 1 = (a + 1)(b + 1). What stays constant?
Near the end: the code starts with 11 and ends with 7. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Smudged Code
story: Part of the code is smudged. Only three digits are readable: 2 _ 9 _ _ 1.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The visible digits are in positions 1, 3 and 6: 2, 9 and 1.
The three missing digits are consecutive whole numbers, increasing from left to right.
All six digits are different.
The six digits add up to 24.

explanation: k + (k + 1) + (k + 2) = 12 so k = 3. Missing digits 3, 4, 5. Code: 239451. The code is 239451.
hints: Call the first missing digit k. What are the other two?
The visible digits sum to 12, so the missing ones sum to 12.
Near the end: the code starts with 23 and ends with 1. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Folded Net
story: A flat net of a cube is folded. Opposite faces end up at opposite sides.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Fold the net into a cube. The code gives, for faces 1 to 6 in order, the number on the face directly opposite.

explanation: Opposites: 1-6, 2-4, 3-5. Code: 645231. The code is 645231.
hints: In a straight row of four faces, faces two apart are opposite.
The vertical strip 1-3-6 closes a ring with face 5: so 1 is opposite 6.
Near the end: the code starts with 64 and ends with 1. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Keypad Cipher
story: A word is hidden twice over: FLSKHU.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Stage one: each letter of FLSKHU was moved forward 3 places. Undo it.
Stage two: type the real word on an old phone keypad (2 = ABC, 3 = DEF, 4 = GHI, 5 = JKL, 6 = MNO, 7 = PQRS, 8 = TUV, 9 = WXYZ). The digits you would press are the code.

explanation: FLSKHU -> CIPHER. Keys: 247437. The code is 247437.
hints: Shift each letter back by three before anything else.
FLSKHU becomes CIPHER. C is on key 2.
Near the end: the code starts with 24 and ends with 7. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Chinese Remainders
story: Three pairs each satisfy a system of remainder rules.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: leaves remainder 2 mod 3, remainder 3 mod 5, remainder 2 mod 7.
Middle pair: remainder 1 mod 4, remainder 2 mod 5, remainder 3 mod 7.
Last pair: remainder 4 mod 5, remainder 5 mod 6, remainder 1 mod 7.

explanation: 23, 17 and 29. The code is 231729.
hints: Start with the largest modulus and list numbers with that remainder.
For the last pair, 4 mod 5 and 5 mod 6 together mean the number is 29 mod 30.
Near the end: the code starts with 23 and ends with 9. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Backward Chain
story: Each digit is defined by the ones to its right. Start at the end.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The first digit is the second plus the third, minus 4.
The second digit is three less than the third.
The third digit is the fifth plus the fourth, minus the last.
The fourth digit is twice the last digit.
The fifth digit is the fourth plus the last.
The last digit is the only even prime number.

hints: Find the clue that does not depend on any other digit.
Last = 2, then fourth, then fifth, then third, second, first.
Near the end: the code starts with 95 and ends with 2. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Zigzag
story: Six numbered tiles (1 to 6) must be placed in a zigzag pattern.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The code uses each digit 1 to 6 exactly once.
The digits go up, down, up, down, up: first < second > third < fourth > fifth < sixth.
The first digit is 2, the third is 1, and the last is 6.
The second digit is exactly one more than the fourth digit.

explanation: Options for (2nd, 4th, 5th): (5,4,3), (4,5,3), (3,5,4). Second = fourth + 1 leaves (5,4,3). Code: 251436. The code is 251436.
hints: Place the three fixed digits first.
The remaining digits are 3, 4 and 5 for positions 2, 4, 5. Position 4 must beat position 5.
Near the end: the code starts with 25 and ends with 6. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Spiral Out
story: A 5 x 5 grid of digits sits on the vault floor.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Start at the centre cell. Move 1 step right, 1 step down, 2 left, 2 up, 3 right, 3 down, and so on, spiralling outward.
The code is the first six cells you stand on (including the centre), in order.

explanation: Cells visited give 492851. The code is 492851.
hints: Mark the centre of the 5 x 5 grid first.
Cells in order: centre, right, down, left, left, up.
Near the end: the code starts with 49 and ends with 1. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Say What You See
story: The wall shows 1, 11, 21, 1211, 111221 and stops.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Each term describes the previous term. The code is the next term.

explanation: 111221 is three 1s, two 2s, one 1. Next term: 312211. The code is 312211.
hints: Read 111221 aloud: "three ones, ..."
Group equal digits: 111, 22, 1. Describe each group.
Near the end: the code starts with 31 and ends with 1. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Three Riddles II
story: Three independent riddles each yield a pair.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: a two-digit number whose digits add up to 11, and which is 27 less than its reversal.
Middle pair: a perfect square whose two digits multiply to 18.
Last pair: the largest two-digit multiple of 13 whose digits are consecutive numbers.

hints: Treat each riddle separately.
First: reversal minus number is 9 times the digit difference. Second: list two-digit squares. Third: list multiples of 13.
Near the end: the code starts with 47 and ends with 8. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Gray Matter
story: A Gray-coded display flashes: 0111 0000 0010 1101 0100 0011.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Gray code: the first bit of the binary number is copied; each later binary bit is the previous binary bit XOR the current Gray bit.
Convert each 4-bit Gray word to ordinary binary, then to a decimal digit. The six digits are the code.

explanation: Binary words decode to 503972. The code is 503972.
hints: Convert the first word: 0111. The first bit is 0.
Binary bits: 0, then 0 XOR 1 = 1, then 1 XOR 1 = 0, then 0 XOR 1 = 1.
Near the end: the code starts with 50 and ends with 2. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Self-Describing
story: Each digit of the code counts something about the whole code.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The first digit is the number of even digits in the code (0 counts as even).
The second digit is the number of odd digits in the code.
The third digit is the number of digits that are 5 or greater.
The fourth digit is the number of zeros in the code.
The fifth digit is the number of twos in the code.
The last digit is the number of digits that are less than 3.

explanation: Assume 4 even, 2 odd digits; the digits are 4, 2, 0, 1, 1, 4. Check each statement: 4 evens, 2 odds, no digit 5+, one zero, one two, four digits below 3. Code: 420114. The code is 420114.
steps: Assume 4 even, 2 odd digits; the digits are 4, 2, 0, 1, 1, 4.
Check each statement: 4 evens, 2 odds, no digit 5+, one zero, one two, four digits below 3.
hints: Even digits plus odd digits make six in total. What does that say about the first two digits?
The first two digits add up to 6. If no digit is 5 or more, the third digit is 0.
Near the end: the code starts with 42 and ends with 4. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Torch Bridge
story: Four travellers must cross a bridge at night. At most two can cross at once and they must carry the only torch. A pair moves at the speed of the slower walker. The torch must be walked back for others.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Group A takes 1, 2, 5 and 10 minutes to cross alone. Group B takes 1, 3, 6 and 8 minutes.
First pair: the fastest total time for group A to get everyone across.
Middle pair: the fastest total time for group B.
Last pair: the number of one-way trips in the fastest plan for group A.

explanation: Group A: 17 minutes in 5 trips (send 1+2, 1 back, 5+10, 2 back, 1+2). Group B: 18 minutes. The code is 171805.
steps: Group A: 17 minutes in 5 trips (send 1+2, 1 back, 5+10, 2 back, 1+2).
hints: Send the two fastest first. Who should bring the torch back?
Compare two plans: always escort with the fastest walker, versus sending the two slowest together.
Near the end: the code starts with 17 and ends with 5. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Lattice Paths
story: A courier moves only right or down on a grid of streets.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: the number of shortest routes across a 4 x 4 block grid (4 steps right, 4 steps down).
Middle pair: the number of shortest routes across a 3 x 5 grid (5 right, 3 down).
Last pair: the number of shortest routes across a 2 x 2 grid.

hints: Every route is an arrangement of R steps and D steps.
Choose which of the 8 steps are rights: C(8,4) and C(8,3).
Near the end: the code starts with 70 and ends with 6. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Nim Gate
story: Three piles of stones hold 7, 9 and 12. Players take any number of stones from one pile. Whoever takes the last stone wins. You move first and want to win.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: the nim-sum (bitwise XOR) of the three pile sizes.
Middle pair: the number of the only pile (counting 1, 2, 3) where a winning move exists.
Last pair: how many stones that winning move removes.

explanation: Nim-sum = 2. Only pile 1 works: 7 -> 5. Code: 020102. The code is 020102.
hints: A winning move leaves a nim-sum of zero.
7 XOR 9 XOR 12 = 2. A pile p is a candidate if p XOR 2 is smaller than p.
Near the end: the code starts with 02 and ends with 2. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: The Labyrinth
story: The last gate of the chapter ties three pairs together.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The first pair is a perfect square greater than 40.
The last pair is the first pair written backwards, and it is a multiple of 23.
The middle pair is the first pair plus the last pair, divided by 11.

explanation: 46 = 2 x 23, so the first pair is 64. (64 + 46) / 11 = 10. Code: 64 10 46. The code is 641046.
steps: 46 = 2 x 23, so the first pair is 64.
hints: List the squares above 40 and reverse each.
Squares: 49, 64, 81. Reversals: 94, 46, 18. Which is a multiple of 23?
Near the end: the code starts with 64 and ends with 6. Work out the middle three digits yourself.
